All right. So for those of you that are new to CAC, we brought an information report and presentation to this committee in February of 2020 as part of the first phase of the OCP redesign project during the approval process.
And so in June of 2020 council unanimously adopted the official community plan or OCP followed by adoption from the province in August.

So I'd like to return to the question, what is an OCP?

It's a statutory document or legal document that guides the physical environmental, economic, social and cultural development of the city and provide the comprehensive policy framework to shape long term growth.
The adoption of an OCP is mandated by the province through the Planning and Development Act and it grants the city the authority to undertake planning initiatives.
The OCP is meant to be the overarching document that all other management documents aligned with management documents include bylaws, policies, strategies, plans, procedures and guidelines.

The OCP works in conjunction with the city's strategic plan and the multi year business plan and editing process to create a strategic framework for how priorities are set and how the city achieves its goals.

So section C of the OCP is based on the strategic plan. This includes the city's priorities regarding and clean air and water renewable energy sources and green tech compact neighborhood design and account transportation and biodiversity and the protection of natural areas and assets.
Context content that will be discussed in the next couple of slides provide support for these priority areas.

So section E environmental leadership focuses on policies regarding sustainability and the environment. This is largely a new addition to the OCP as there has been significant work done focusing on the environment and sustainability in recent years.
We've seen the adoption or endorsement of the triple bottom line policy, the way some are cycling planned for an infrastructure strategy, the will be mission community plan among others.
This is all very important work that the current OCP provides support for and by creating an entire section devoted to the environment and sustainability.
There is a clear framework to support this ongoing work and future related work.
So section E is broken into six subsections.
Environmental protection includes policies on responsible practices and maintaining the integrity of land, air and water resources in Saskatoon and surrounding region.

The natural system subsection contains policies on storm water management, conservation areas, urban forestry and integration of ecological systems in our urban areas while limiting impacts of development or sensitive areas.
As well as providing support for an asset management policy.

Energy policies support the conservation and efficient use of energy and renewable energy resources along with supporting construction of stable buildings and reducing the impacts of civic buildings as a city is actively trying to meet the mission reduction targets.
Waste management policies outlined how Saskatoon can effectively reduce reuse recycle recover and dispose of waste.
This includes a variety of programs and initiatives including recycling composting and hazardous waste collection.

Climate policies outline the commitment to and implementation of Saskatoon's climate action plan as the city has made a commitment to reducing greenhouse gases and adopting adapting to changing climate conditions.
And lastly, community leadership policies support public engagement outreach education initiatives and program development to foster and informed and engaged community.
It is also important to note that there are other sections and policies found in the OCP that support the environment and sustainability.

The decision-dee quality of life includes policies on food systems that consider the social, cultural environmental and economic impacts of how food is grown process distributed acquired and disposed of in Saskatoon.
